contexts.text: As it comes forth from the Lord in this way, so it also subsists; for subsistence is a perpetual coming forth.
Those in Divine ideas never stop in the objects of external sight.
No evil can subsist (or stay) in a sphere where good is.
Without this marriage, nothing in nature would subsist.
Without a Church somewhere in the world, the human race could not subsist. Explained.
Without this connection (with the Spiritual World), neither man, nor any part of him, could subsist for a moment; for all his subsistence is thence.
From this is the coming forth and subsistence of all things.

The learned know that subsistence is a perpetual coming forth; but still it is contrary to an affection for what is false... to say that nature continually subsists, as it has come forth, from the Divine of the Lord. As, therefore, each and all things subsist from the Divine, that is, continually come forth... it follows that the visible universe is a representative theatre of the Lord's Kingdom...
Nothing can come forth and subsist from itself...

Man believes not in any influx from the Spiritual World... although he might know that nothing can subsist except through [the fact] that it has existed, (or come forth); that is, that subsistence is a perpetual coming forth; or, what is the same, production is continual creation.
There is not anything which can subsist from itself, but from something else; and this again from something else; and, finally, from the First; and this through a connection of correspondences.

All the smallest particulars in man come forth (from the correspondence between Heaven and man), and therefore they also subsist from it; for subsistence is a perpetual coming forth. AC 4525, (See Correspond.)

(Thus) whatever is in the world... does not come forth from itself, but from what is prior to itself; and this... from what is prior to itself; and so on even to the First, from whom the sequents come forth in order. And, as they come forth thence, they also subsist thence; for subsistence is a perpetual coming forth. Hence it follows that each and all things, down to the ultimate things of nature, have not only come forth from the First, but also subsist from the First; for, unless they perpetually came forth, and unless there were a continuous connection from the First, and thus with the First, they would perish in a moment. (Continued. See Exist, at AC 4524.)
They could scarcely subsist for blessedness (there).
Unless there were such a correspondence of man with Heaven, and through Heaven with the Lord, he would not subsist for a single moment. All these things are held in connection by influx. AC 5377:2.
(Such) do not consider that subsistence is a perpetual coming forth; or, what is similar, that propagation is a perpetual creation.

Without correspondence with... the Spiritual World, nothing ever comes forth and subsists, for the reason that it has not any connection with what is prior to itself; nor, consequently, with the First... That which is unconnected, and thus independent, cannot subsist for a single moment; for the reason it subsists is its connection and dependence upon that from which is all existence (or coming forth); for subsistence is a perpetual coming forth.
For to subsist is perpetually to come forth, (Continued from Exist.)

For it is a universal canon that nothing can subsist from itself... So with man: he as to his external cannot subsist except from the internal, and through it; nor can the internal man subsist except from Heaven and through it; and neither can Heaven subsist from itself, but from the Lord, who alone subsists from Himself. Influx is according to existence (or coming forth) and subsistence; for all things subsist through influx. But that each and all things subsist from the Lord through influx, not only mediately through the Spiritual World, but also immediately, in both mediates and ultimates, will be demonstrated in what follows.
Hence it is that every formation comes forth separated from every other; but still so that the posterior depends upon the prior, insomuch that it cannot subsist without the prior...

He does not consider that nothing can subsist unless it perpetually exists (or comes forth); for, as is known in the learned world, subsistence is a perpetual coming forth; thus conservation is a perpetual creation.
Unless this were so, a formed thing could not possibly subsist and act.
An Earth could not subsist without a human race. Explained.
All things subsist through the Divine truth. (See Exist.)

All things in Heaven come forth according to this order, and subsist according to the same; for to subsist is to perpetually exist (or come forth). In order, therefore, that Heaven may come forth in man, it is necessary that he receive the Divine truth...
In the ultimate, interior things subsist and quiesce.

Everything unconnected with the Divine perishes... Nothing can ever come forth without what is prior to itself, thus without the Divine... consequently it cannot subsist; for to subsist is to perpetually come forth.
Thus the consistence and subsistence of Heaven. Signified, Explained.

Existence and subsistence in perpetuity and without change. Signified. For through the Divine sphere... Heaven has come into existence and was created; and through the same it subsists and is conserved; for subsistence is a perpetual coming forth; and conservation is a perpetual creation.

As celestial good thus comes forth through truths in their order, so it afterwards subsists in the like order through the same truths; for subsistence is a perpetual coming forth. And, when it subsists just as it had come forth it is complete; for then the higher things subsist, rest, and repose themselves in order upon the lower things as upon their planes; and upon the extremes or ultimates, which are sensuous scientific truths, as upon their foundation.
Hence the connection of all things, and the influx according to the connection, and the consequent subsistence of one thing from another.
For to subsist is perpetually to come forth.
From this correspondence, man subsists; for man subsists from no other source than Heaven.
Thus it is the Corporeal of man... upon which, as upon its basis, Heaven subsists.

All things which come forth in nature... are correspondences; (for the reason that) the natural world... comes forth and subsists from the Spiritual World; and both from the Divine. It is said that it also subsists, because everything subsists from that from which it comes forth; for subsistence is a perpetual coming forth; and because not anything can subsist from itself, but from what is prior to itself, thus from the First; and therefore, if it is separated from this, it entirely perishes and vanishes away.
They stop at the first step.
Every Spirit... subsists by influx from (the Society to which he belongs).
Mediate influx subsists through immediate influx.
The conjunction of Heaven with the human race, and of this with Heaven, is such, that the one subsists from the other. LJ 9:8.

They know, when they think, that nothing can subsist from itself, but from what is prior to itself, thus all things from a First; and that the connection with what is prior to itself is like that of an effect with its effecting cause. (Continued. See Exist.)
Divine order never halts in the middle...
Infants (there) do not advance beyond early youth, but remain in it to all eternity. CL 411:2. CL 444:end. Explained.
An equilibrium in which all things subsist.
Creation... proceeded to its ultimates, and then first subsisted.
When man (becomes a Spirit) he does not subsist upon his Own basis; but upon the general basis, which is the human race.
No Angel or Spirit can subsist without man; and no man without Spirit and Angel. (Thus) the human race and the angelic Heaven make a one, and they subsist mutually from each other...

The sun (must be) the first of creation; for all things in its world subsist from it; and, because they subsist from it, they have existed (or come forth) from it. The one involves and bears witness to the other. For all things are under the sun's view, because it determined that they should be; and to keep under its view is to determine continually; and therefore, also, it is said, that subsistence is a perpetual coming forth. Explained.
There are such things (as spaces), because creation ceased there, and subsists in its state of rest.
For sustentation is perpetual creation; as subsistence is a perpetual coming forth.
The Angels (then) cannot remain in their state of love and wisdom.

The reason the Church in the Heavens does not subsist unless it has been conjoined with a Church on earth. Explained... The internal with man does not subsist in its state, unless the external is conjoined with it. Explained.
For thus subsistence or conservation is perpetual coming forth, or creation.
Ends progress... down to the terminus, in which they subsist or cease.
As (evil) does not prevail against good, it stops in the endeavour.
Every man becomes... successively rational; and, if he does not bait there, he becomes spiritual.

That the world has come forth from the sun, and not the converse, is evident from the effect of the cause, in that the world in each and all things of it subsists by means of the sun; and subsistence demonstrates coming forth; and therefore it is said that subsistence is a perpetual coming forth... ISB 9.
That... through the (natural) sun the world of nature has come forth and subsists. General article.
The man who halts in the first state... is like...
Without that Redemption... the Angels would not have been able to stay in a state of integrity. General article. TCR 579.
If this were done, both (the heart and lungs) would stop.
Would not his thought (then) come to a stand?
In elevation as to the understanding, while the love of the will stays below...

Interiors are distinct from exteriors thus: that the former can come forth and subsist, without the latter; but not the converse; for exteriors come forth from their interiors. For... all things come forth from an inmost or first, as from their simple; and, because they come forth from it, they also subsist from it; for subsistence is a perpetual coming forth.
Perpetual coming forth; that is, subsistence...
They halt at the ninth use.
For without a Church... the world cannot subsist. Explained.

For the Heavens subsist upon the human race as a house on its foundation; and hence the wisdom of the Angels in like manner subsist upon the knowledge, intelligence, and wisdom of men from the sense of the letter...
Lastly, the terraqueous globe was created, in order that there might be ultimate matters there, into which everything spiritual might cease, and in which creation might subsist...
Yet it is an eternal truth... that sustentation is perpetual creation, as subsistence is perpetual existence (or coming forth).

All the Celestial inflows into the Spiritual; and the Spiritual into the Natural; and, into the ultimate of this, which is the Corporeal and Material, it ceases, and there subsists. Without such an ultimate, into which the intermediates may inflow, subsistence is impossible...
7. That from this Spirits and Angels derive the ability to subsist and live to eternity. Explained.
